Use this pathway after the normal electronics teaching and problem set. The notebooks support the circuit model; they do not replace deriving equations, building safely, or measuring a real system.

::: {.callout-note title="Current class position"}
Basic schematics and the five KCL/KVL questions are complete. Before circuit linear algebra, students begin with a zero-experience Python notebook, then learn NumPy, plotting, documentation lookup, and evidence-based help requests. The bridge is **run one line → variables and types → lists → one small array → NumPy investigation → Kirchhoff equations → matrix model**. Capacitors and RC response follow this bridge.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Browser start: open JupyterLite"}
**JupyterLite is the browser program that runs the downloaded notebook.** Click **[OPEN JUPYTERLITE NOW](https://jupyter.org/try-jupyter/lab/){target="_blank"}**, use **Upload Files**, and double-click the downloaded `.ipynb` file. Use the [step-by-step JupyterLite instructions](jupyterlite.qmd) if this is your first notebook.
:::

1. [Read the step-by-step JupyterLite instructions](jupyterlite.qmd): download a notebook, open JupyterLite, upload the file, run a cell, and preserve the finished work.
2. [Play Circuit Quest](circuit-quest.qmd): rotate circuit tiles, complete paths, light lamps, and power a branch.
3. [Complete Python First Steps](python-first-steps.qmd): print one line, use calculator operations, store variables, recognize types, select list items, and use one small NumPy array.
4. [Run Python and Jupyter on your own computer](local-python-jupyter.qmd): use a virtual environment in WSL, native Windows, macOS, or Linux instead of depending on JupyterLite.
5. [Complete Python and NumPy Foundations](python-numpy-foundations.qmd): practise loops, functions, arrays, filters, checks, plotting, and one documentation-driven repair.
6. [Find documentation and ask for programming help](finding-documentation-and-asking-for-help.qmd): reproduce an issue, search Python, NumPy, pandas, and Stack Overflow, and write a complete technical help request.
7. [Complete the two-loops-to-matrix assignment](kirchhoff-jupyter-assignment.qmd): derive each loop equation step by step, build the matrix, and compare NumPy with an exact SymPy solution.
8. [Work through the Jupyter Electronics Lab](jupyter-electronics-lab.qmd): apply the skills across KCL/KVL, graphs, data, investigation, RC, op-amps, and the calculus bridge.
9. [Complete the Life Checkpoint Upgrade](midterm-circuit-investigation.qmd): digitize and correct the checkpoint, solve it with NumPy, and verify the same circuit in Tinkercad.
10. Continue to [Python measurement logging](../linux-operating-systems/python-data-logging.qmd) and [analysis and curve fitting](../linux-operating-systems/python-analysis-curve-fitting.qmd) when the investigation needs repeated measurements or a fitted model.

::: {.callout-important title="Current assignment"}
Begin with [Circuit Quest](circuit-quest.qmd), then use the same [Life Checkpoint Upgrade: Jupyter + Tinkercad](midterm-circuit-investigation.qmd) notebook on Monday and Tuesday. Submit the notebook, Tinkercad URL, screenshot, and any missing course work through the assigned Classroom posts. Use [Python First Steps](python-first-steps.qmd), [Python and NumPy Foundations](python-numpy-foundations.qmd), and [From Two Loops to a Matrix](kirchhoff-jupyter-assignment.qmd) as support or catch-up work.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Core workflow"}
**Understand → Calculate → Build → Simulate → Measure → Verify → Investigate → Document → Share**

Most introductory notebook activities take about 15–30 minutes after the electronics calculation is complete. The [Jupyter Electronics Lab](jupyter-electronics-lab.qmd) also defines multi-day investigations that can carry the electronics course while students wait for components, instruments, or soldered kits.
:::

The browser route does not require a local installation or a new account, but the school browser must allow JupyterLite and WebAssembly. Download work before leaving the browser.

Hardware remains valuable, but it is not assumed to be simultaneously available to every student. A simulation-first submission is complete when it meets the stated modelling outcomes and labels its evidence honestly. Measurements can be added later as a separate validation stage.
